dimensions.rationale: The main sequence is clear, but oversized low-information KPI cards and repeated high-emphasis treatments keep the page below a consistently premium standard.
Six deep KPI cards communicate one value each, while the drilldown uses oversized repetitive hourly cards that are inefficient for comparison.
Core controls are recognizable, but heavily muted range actions and uniformly emphasized export selections weaken state hierarchy.
Active and selected states are visible, but inactive controls are faint and the drilldown does not strongly link its chart and selected-slice summary.
The overview and PDF modal are coherent, but the drilldown has mismatched density and visibly continues beyond the modal without a polished continuation cue.
Core headings are readable, while secondary labels, chart ticks, and control states remain small or muted across dark surfaces.
The page is recognizably FitTrack, but repeated outlined rectangles and saturated orange selections reduce professional restraint.

findings.observation: Each KPI card separates its label and value with a large empty region while providing no supporting context.
findings.user_impact: Administrators scan six visually large surfaces but receive little information, pushing substantive insight content downward.
findings.repair_direction: Reduce card height and tighten label-value proximity without inventing unsupported trend data.
findings.verification: The six-card block occupies materially less vertical space in full and compact states while preserving value prominence.

findings.observation: The drilldown pairs a sparse chart with a long column of oversized hourly cards and clips continuing content.
findings.user_impact: Peak-hour comparison requires unnecessary scrolling and the modal appears unfinished.
findings.repair_direction: Use compact comparable rows and an unmistakable bounded scroll treatment.
findings.verification: More hourly data is visible at once and any continuing content has an obvious scroll boundary.

findings.observation: Range actions and several inactive labels use similarly subdued treatments.
findings.user_impact: Enabled, disabled, active, and secondary states are harder to distinguish at a glance.
findings.repair_direction: Reserve strong muting for disabled states and preserve clear interactive hierarchy.
findings.verification: Control states are immediately distinguishable in full and compact captures.

findings.observation: Every selected PDF section uses a saturated orange border, creating eight equally emphatic tiles.
findings.user_impact: The modal loses restraint and competes with its primary export action.
findings.repair_direction: Use a quieter selected surface while keeping the checkbox as the primary marker.
findings.verification: Selections remain clear while Export PDF is the dominant orange action.

dimensions.rationale: The page sequence is clear, but oversized KPI cards, subdued section labels, and a detached attendance action weaken scanning efficiency.
Headline metrics are easy to scan but consume substantial space for one value, and repeated drilldown records expose little comparative information.
Date, tab, PDF, and close controls are recognizable, but the attendance action is weakly associated and the drilldown lacks a continuation affordance.
Applied range and selection states are visible, while raw fallback amounts and limited drilldown labeling reduce professional comprehension.
Full and compact layouts preserve their grid and the PDF modal is coherent, but the drilldown ends with a cropped record and no clear internal-scroll treatment.
Large headings and values are readable, while numerous secondary labels and state distinctions are small, low-contrast, or color-dependent.
The visual language is FitTrack-consistent, but the analytics treatment remains generic and short on gym-operational interpretation.

findings.observation: The peak-hour column visibly continues beyond the modal boundary with no scrollbar, fade, footer, or continuation cue.
findings.user_impact: Administrators may not realize more hourly data exists or how to reach it.
findings.repair_direction: Give the detail area an unmistakable bounded scroll treatment or fit the essential summary content.
findings.verification: Any additional hourly entries have an immediately recognizable continuation affordance.

findings.observation: Section labels, tab captions, descriptions, chart labels, and several controls use small subdued gray text on dark surfaces.
findings.user_impact: Scanning and control recognition become unnecessarily difficult in compact and modal states.
findings.repair_direction: Raise secondary-text contrast and minimum readable size without overwhelming the hierarchy.
findings.verification: Secondary content remains readily readable in all supplied states without close inspection.

findings.observation: Fallback insight values are shown as raw decimals rather than using the localized formats in the KPI cards.
findings.user_impact: The state appears machine-generated and reduces trust and comprehension.
findings.repair_direction: Apply the same localized currency and number formatting used by corresponding metrics.
findings.verification: Fallback values match the recognizable format of the dashboard metrics.
